Sports.title: Marcus Rashford thanks Jamie Carragher for NOT talking about him... after Gary Neville pushed to discuss his Man United future
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford thanks Jamie Carragher for NOT talking about him... after Gary Neville pushed to discuss his Man United future

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Marcus Rashford has thanked Jamie Carragher for shutting down talk about his future at Man United after Gary Neville was keen to dig into the subject.

The England international returned to Old Trafford after his Barcelona loan expired and his £325,000-a-week wages have made it tricky to find a new club.

Last year, it seems incredibly unlikely that Rashford would be able to settle back at Man United again but he featured in their last pre-season friendly and looks set for reintegration.

On The Overlap Fan Debate, brought to you by Sky Bet, there was a terse but light-hearted exchange between Carragher and Neville.

The Liverpool legend lamented: 'Oh f***ing hell. Can we do a podcast without mentioning Rashford? Stop it! Oh my god. It’s like the Trent and Rashford - there was like a little part of the podcast - the Trent part or the Rashford part.'

Neville then joked: 'How is Trent?'

Marcus Rashford is back at Man United having been on loan with Barcelona last season

Carragher was frustrated at the repeated discussion of Rashford by Gary Neville

Thanks, Jamie. It would be great to be able to get my head down and play football without my name being mentioned every day 😭 https://t.co/GTqrKhbZEE — MR (@MarcusRashford) August 19, 2026

Carragher: 'Oh my God.'

Neville: 'No, but he’s come back to United.'

Carragher: 'So what? Oh my God. He’s just a good player for Man United!'

The clip was then posted on social media and Rashford himself saw it, prompting him to comment.

He wrote: 'Thanks, Jamie. It would be great to be able to get my head down and play football without my name being mentioned every day.'

Rashford was disappointed Barcelona chose not to trigger the £26m option they had to buy him in the summer.

Instead, the club splashed out £69m on his England team-mate Anthony Gordon from Newcastle.

Unless a club come in for Rashford in the final two weeks of the transfer window, he will remain at United.

The 28-year-old could yet force his way into Carrick's starting line-up and the manager said: 'He's a very good player, and I think if you're going to have a career over 10 or 15 years, there's going to be times when things go in a direction and maybe a different direction.

'I think there are ups and downs, and that doesn't judge you as a one-off kind of judgment. It's what happens over time, and now we're in a positive place as a group, and Marcus can offer us so much. He has done, and he can do again, so in that respect, it's quite exciting.

'He came in, he's trained really well. I've known him a long time, like I've known some of the others a long time, so I don't treat him any different to anybody else, but it's been good to have him around the group again this week. So I'm really positive with that.'

Sports.title: Now Man City turn to France midfielder Manu Kone - a target for rivals United this summer - as their post-Pep revolution gathers pace
Sports.content:
Manchester City have identified Roma’s Manu Kone as a potential signing for their revamped midfield after selling Rodri and Tijjani Reijnders.

Both midfielders departed this week for a combined total of around £110million, leaving Enzo Maresca with holes to fill in his squad just days before the Premier League season starts.

City are hopeful of wrapping up a deal for Lille’s deep-lying midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, valued at £85m, in the coming days to bolster that area of the pitch.

And Daily Mail Sport understands that Kone – who featured five times for France during the World Cup – is on the list of those to target before the window closes.

The 25-year-old has spent the past two years in Serie A, scoring four goals in 63 appearances for Roma, but is more renowned for his dynamism and excels off the ball.

Roma are reported to have set an asking price of around £51m for Kone – a broadly similar figure to that paid by Al-Qadsiah for Reijnders.

Both Chelsea and Manchester United have been linked with the former Borussia Monchengladbach man. Daily Mail Sport last month revealed how United had spoken to his representatives, but they are now swooping for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba.

Roma midfielder Manu Kone featured five times for France during the World Cup and is now on Manchester City's list of targets for the summer

Kone, who has 19 caps for France, started four of their matches in North America over the summer and came on at half time in their semi-final defeat by Spain.

City remain interested in Enzo Fernandez, with Chelsea’s soft deadline to complete a deal for £120m having passed without a formal bid. The Argentina midfielder wants to link back up with Maresca but City are unwilling to reach Chelsea’s demands.

In what promises to be a frantic final fortnight of the window, Newcastle are also exploring a move for Nico Gonzalez.

City are in advanced talks to sell both Savinho and Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

The two deals combined would likely be worth upwards of £140m, with Daily Mail Sport revealing earlier in the week that Spurs were pressing ahead with those moves.

Maresca recently suggested that both players were considering their futures after a lack of minutes last term.

Sports.title: Curtis Jones edging towards £30m transfer from Liverpool to Inter Milan - as the third member of Italian giants' English revolution this summer
Sports.content:
Inter Milan are on the verge of signing Liverpool midfielder Curtis Jones after a summer-long back and forth.

The six-time England international, who joined Liverpool aged nine, has had his heart set on a move to Serie A for some time after failing to regularly establish himself as a starter at Anfield.

And it now appears he will leave, with the two clubs in dialogue. A fee of around £30million is likely to get the deal done, and Daily Mail Sport understands the Italian club have offered £26.7.m plus £4m in add-ons, with a 10 per cent sell-on clause.

The Italian champions had a bid of around £21m turned down earlier in the summer and, if they sign Jones, he will be the third Englishman they have bought this window after Manchester City's John Stones and Tottenham's Djed Spence.

Liverpool meanwhile are preparing for their first season under new manager Andoni Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot following the Dutchman's dismissal at the end of last season.

The six-time England international, who joined Liverpool aged nine, has had his heart set on a move to Serie A for some time after failing to regularly establish himself as a starter at Anfield

It appears Jones will follow Tottenham's Djed Spence as an Englishman heading to Inter

John Stones also moved to the San Siro on a free transfer from Manchester City this summer

The Italian press expect an official announcement on Jones to follow and say a medical has already been scheduled for him.

After spending over £450million on new signings including Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer, the 2024-25 Premier League champions struggled to reach the same heights again under the Dutchman and only narrowly managed to qualify for the Champions League with a fifth-place finish last term.

Liverpool, who waved farewell to Mohamed Salah, Andrew Robertson and Ibrahima Konate at the start of the summer, have so far recruited centre-half Jeremy Jacquet from Stade Rennais and left winger Victor Munoz from Osasuna ahead of the new campaign.

While theoretically all first-team places are up for grabs under new boss Iraola, Jones has been viewed as a squad player at the club in recent seasons, playing second fiddle to fellow central midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexis Mac Allister, Ryan Gravenberch and Wirtz under Slot and previously Jurgen Klopp.

Sports.title: Premier League chief insists Man City's 115 charges saga is 'NOT top of the list' in conversations with rival clubs - and adds verdict will take 'as long as it takes'
Sports.content:
Premier League chief insists Man City's 115 charges saga is 'NOT top of the list' in conversations with rival clubs - and adds verdict will take 'as long as it takes'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Premier League boss Richard Masters has claimed that Manchester City’s ongoing 115 charges saga is ‘not necessarily top of the list’ when it comes to his conversations with clubs.

City’s trial – over allegations of repeated breaches of the top-flight’s financial controls – ended in December 2024 but an eagerly-awaited verdict remains outstanding, despite the fact it is now well over three years since they were originally charged.

Four Premier League sides have reserved the right to seek compensation should City be found guilty and it would appear that much of football is desperate for an outcome.

However, Masters suggested that the noise in boardrooms up and down the country is not as loud as one might imagine.

‘I obviously speak to clubs all the time,’ he said. ‘It's not necessarily a topic of conversation that is top of the list. (There are) Lots of other things to talk about and do. The Premier League moves on. It's starting (again) on Friday evening.’

Masters has previously admitted to being frustrated by the length of time the independent panel is taking to return its verdict, which could see City exonerated or facing historic penalties.

Premier League boss Richard Masters has claimed that Manchester City’s ongoing 115 charges saga is ‘not necessarily top of the list’ when it comes to his conversations with clubs

City’s trial – over allegations of repeated breaches of the top-flight’s financial controls – ended in December 2024 but a verdict remains outstanding. City deny all wrongdoing

‘The process is the process,’ he said. ‘It will resolve itself. But as you know, I literally can't say a thing about it. There's only one available option, which is to allow the process to reach its natural conclusion. I can't talk about the substance of the case. I can't talk about the timing of the case. Our rules are very clear about that. I understand that people are frustrated but it will take as long as it takes.’

The Premier League’s latest domestic broadcast deal has seen the amount paid per game fall by around £2.5m.

Some have wondered if that is an indicator that fans are getting fed up of various litigations, with Nottingham Forest, Everton and Leicester City docked points in recent times.

But when asked if the perceived lenient penalty, a £10m fine handed to Chelsea for repeated backhanders, suggested there was a desire to move on from docking points, Masters denied that was the case.

‘I don't think litigation and broadcast deals are necessarily associated,’ he said. ‘I do think litigation is to be avoided.

‘It should be a last resort within a league system or generally. I think that is generally the attitude that is taken by stakeholders in the game. Litigation is a last resort.’

Sports.title: Inside Arsenal's Title-Winning Season: Exclusive book extract reveals how Mikel Arteta's man-management skills ended 22-year wait for the title
Sports.content:
On the final day of the season, Martin Odegaard was one of the last players to make his way off the Selhurst Park turf with the Premier League trophy in his hands.

Photographers commissioned by the league had already snapped the rest of the team individually and were waiting for the captain. As Odegaard spoke to photographers about getting his picture taken, an Arsenal staff member pulled the trophy off him, telling the Norwegian that 'the boss wants it (the trophy)' before quickly carrying it over to Mikel Arteta.

Even in success, there was one man who superseded it all. The power a manager wields at a football club is complex. It's not linear. It grows over time and shows itself in differing ways. In the Premier League, the power Arteta holds at Arsenal is of a rarer kind.

By the 2025-26 season, that influence was ever-present. This had not always been the case. When he arrived in December 2019, Arteta was a novice head coach inheriting a fractured environment. Authority, at that point, was something to be earned.

Over time, he imposed it, transforming Arsenal into a club shaped in his own image. The results were there to be seen: the players all respected him and there was no stepping out of line. If they did, a place on the outer perimeter would be the consequence. You either brought into the 'non-negotiables' or faced the sidelines.

There was no room for individual ego. Arteta's focus and determination is admirable, particularly in the context of his own playing career. He only won two league titles: the French Division 1 (now Ligue 1, 2001-02) and the Scottish Premier League at Rangers (2002-03). In his 11 years in England playing for Arsenal and Everton, he won the FA Cup twice – but no league trophy.

Mikel Arteta led Arsenal to their first Premier League triumph since 2004 last season

As someone who craved winning, this was short of what he desired. Going into management, he had to rebuild Arsenal before dreaming of major silverware. Finishing runners-up for three consecutive seasons had taken its toll. That's not easy to accept, nor particularly healthy given the strain on a man obsessed with the objective at hand. Yet he was still able to muster the fortitude to get to the training ground – usually at 7 am – with the belief that this season would be Arsenal's at the fourth time of asking.

Inside the training ground, Arteta's influence extended far beyond tactics. After winning the FA Cup against Chelsea in 2020, the club decided to upgrade him to 'manager' from 'head coach'. As one of just six 'managers' in the league – the other 14 are titled 'head coaches' – he held most of the keys. Departments that at many clubs operate with a degree of independence – sports science and performance analysis, for example – would report directly to the manager.

Staff presented their own work, but the feedback loop was clear. Arteta listened, questioned and then decided. What aligned with his vision stayed. What didn't was adjusted. To the outside, this looked controlling.

On the inside, in the club's view, this was a man with a clear vision, and for it to succeed, everything else had to be in sync. This was particularly significant when it came to matters such as player workload. Arteta took on board the feedback from the sports science department, for example, but had a key say on how often players train and to what intensity.

This is different to clubs with a head coach, where departments often operate independently and report upwards rather than to the coach, who is left only with the tools afforded to them. It's a luxury many bosses in football crave but rarely get the opportunity to have. For Arteta, it was expected.

When discussions emerged around the possibility of expanding the Emirates, driven by sustained demand and waiting lists exceeding 20 years, Arteta was included – not as a technical expert but as a central figure whose perspective carried weight. The stadium was part of the club's identity and therefore part of his domain.

Every process and every structure linked back to Arteta. The benefits were clear: consistency and purpose. But it also meant that any future transition would be complex. Replacing Arteta would not be a simple managerial change. It would require dismantling and rebuilding much of what had been put in place, ripping out the floorboards.

It was working. Winning softened the edges, but in moments of scrutiny his approach rarely shifted. He occasionally arrived late to press conferences to the tune of half an hour – officially because training had overrun. On one afternoon, as journalists sat down having put their recording devices on the desk in front of Arteta, he leaned toward the press officer beside him and whispered, 'What time was this supposed to start?' It was delivered quietly, but the message was clear: he would arrive on his own terms, a reminder that the media's deadlines were completely secondary to the tactical fine-tuning happening out on the pitches.

Some managers embraced these conferences as performance, while others treated them as obligation. Arteta belonged firmly to the latter camp unless he had a specific message to deliver, often doing his utmost to whip the supporters up.

Yet he was unwavering in not letting the press encroach into team matters. Before a January match, Arteta listed William Saliba as doubtful due to injury, though a source confirmed shortly after the conference that he would be available. These injury mind games would be a theme that played out across the campaign.

Arteta often used this tactic deliberately to mask the fitness of key players. It was less deception and more secrecy under the veil of controlling the narrative and protecting his players; he wanted opponents to have no idea of his starting XI until the team-sheet arrived on matchday. 'We will have to wait and see' or 'we are waiting for the training session later' were the go-to answers.

Any further pressing questions would widen his grin – but never his answers. It became a running joke among the press pack, a theatrical routine where we would probe for specifics on hamstrings and ankles, only to be met with that enigmatic, unblinking smile. He took a pleasure in the misdirection, viewing it as a vital layer of his tactical preparation.

To him, even a minor disclosure about a player's fitness was giving an opposing manager a headstart on their team shape. This obsession with information control extended across the premises, with staff tightly briefed on not allowing injury news slip out.

Details mattered, and Arteta had a meticulous eye for the minutiae. He had to fiddle with the microphone upon sitting down in press conferences. Small things – seating arrangements in press rooms, the positioning of equipment – were noticed. Nothing was too minor to escape attention.

On one occasion, a familiar journalist sitting in an unusual position prompted a moment of visible distraction. As he asked a question, Arteta injected, pointing to his right and said, 'You changed your seat.'

Arteta is a great man-manager, he welcomed David Raya and his family with a special touch

The environment was expected not to drift too far from his usual structure. During pre-season tours, that vigilance extended beyond the pitch. On a tour, some staff were wary of eating unhealthy food around the camp in case Arteta noticed. They did not want a stern stare or a quiet word in response. That same instinct extended to day-to-day operations.

There were also lighter touches. He is a caring man, too. In a previous season when one staff member's son was being bullied at school, Arteta invited him in to meet the players and use the gym in the evenings to build his confidence. He is conscious of lifting players.

If he senses someone needs to be picked up, he will always try to do so, whether with an arm around the shoulder or a thoughtful gesture. When David Raya was signed, he invited the Raya family to the stadium and had a custom shirt made for the goalkeeper's grandfather, Joaquin.

It is these moments which made the team want to fight to the end for him.

It is Arteta's balance between intensity and empathy which wrapped Arsenal's players and executives under his spell. For a man who seeks personal connection, those inside his inner circle are treated like family.

Arteta's control and methods were working to great effect in October. Six games, six wins. Liverpool, the league favourites among many pundits at the start of the season, were already being overtaken in the odds. Arsenal recorded 1-0 victories over Crystal Palace and Fulham. Steady displays. Three points on the board. After a testing September, the results were welcome – and needed. The consistent dropping of points is an unhealthy habit and can often prove terminal, no matter how early on in a campaign.

It was the latest evidence of how far Arteta had dragged the club. Those difficult calls and unpopular decisions had paid off, transforming Arsenal into a team capable of downing Europe's elite; a product of Arteta's long-held self-belief that rejected any glimmer of doubt, even when obstacles muddied the course. As the victories mounted across a flawless October, so too did the sense that Arsenal had become a complete reflection of their manager.

Extracted from 22 Years: The Inside Story of Arsenal's Title-Winning Season by Isaan Khan (Biteback Publishing), out August 25. To order a copy go to https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/1837360863

Sports.title: Tottenham push on with moves for City duo Marmoush and Savinho, Aston Villa face competition for Tosin Adarabioyo... and Newcastle are offered former Blues forward Christopher Nkunku: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Tottenham push on with moves for City duo Marmoush and Savinho, Aston Villa face competition for Tosin Adarabioyo... and Newcastle are offered former Blues forward Christopher Nkunku: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Inter hopeful of deal for Jones

Liverpool and Inter Milan have resumed talks over a deal for Curtis Jones today, initiated by the Italian side.

There is currently no agreement for the 25-year-old but terms are being discussed, with Inter having bid £26.7m plus £4m in add-ons and a 10 per cent sell-on clause.

That is similar to the package and structure Inter utilised to sign Tottenham defender Djed Spence, a deal reaching €35m (£30m).

Palace say no to Sarr approach

Crystal Palace have rejected an approach of more than £30m from Galatasaray for Ismaila Sarr. Palace are also braced for offers for Adam Wharton.

BOBBY MANZI

Wrexham aim high with look at Leeds star Lucas

Wrexham are showing interest in an ambitious move for Leeds United forward Lukas Nmecha.

The 27-year-old joined Leeds last summer from Wolfsburg and scored seven goals in 37 appearances.

The Welsh side are also exploring a deal for free agent centre-back and Congo international Axel Tuanzebe.

Spurs push on with Marmoush and Savinho swoops

Tottenham are continuing negotiations with Manchester City over the double deal of Savinho and Omar Marmoush.

As Daily Mail Sport previously revealed, Spurs have identified the Brazilian winger and Egyptian forward as two targets for their forward line along with Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo.

The deal with City would not be cheap, however, while coach Enzo Maresca also wants to ensure he has enough bodies with Jeremy Doku out for the start of the season.

Liverpool, meanwhile, need to ensure they strengthen their own attacking options before allowing anyone to leave and would want a considerable fee to even consider selling Gakpo. Tottenham have made their interest known.

Villa and Marseille keen on Chelsea's Tosin - after he loses No4 shirt

Aston Villa hold interest in Chelsea defender Tosin Adarabioyo but face competition from Marseille.

Adarabioyo is one of a number of options being considered by Unai Emery.

The 6ft 5ins centre-back had been willing to stay at Stamford Bridge and fight for his place but it is becoming apparent it would be in his career's best interests to explore a move away where he would have a more prominent role.

Villa have been assessing names throughout the window after it became clear Arsenal would pursue Ezri Konsa who is likely to wrap up his £51m move to the champions by the weekend.

Adarabioyo also has other other clubs to consider.

Marseille have made contact with Chelsea and are deemed most likely to pursue a move as it stands.

Tosin Adarabioyo signs a shirt for a fan in Hong Kong on Chelsea's pre-season tour

Sevilla are also keen as are Marco Silva's Benfica but are not considered as strong as Marseille and Villa.

Other clubs are also now showing interest in the 28-year-old who joined as a free agent after leaving Fulham in 2024.

In another ominous sign, Adarabioyo has also lost his shirt number in a squad list reshuffle.

Formerly No 4, Adarabioyo will now wear No 38. New signing Valentin Barco takes his old shirt.

Liam Delap is no longer No 9 and will wear No 12,with Joao Pedro taking the No 9.

Chslsea bag Hearts' Osborne

Chelsea have signed 17-year-old centre-back Alfie Osborne from Hearts for £400,000.

Osborne captained Hearts’ U18s to the Scottish FA Youth Cup and has also captained Scotland's U19s.

Reijnders seals Saudi move

Manchester City midfielder Tijjani Reijnders has joined Al Qadsiah for £52m.

Reijnders will work under Brendan Rodgers at Al Qadsiah.

The 28-year-old, who has an offer from Nottingham Forest also, only joined City from AC Milan last summer for £46.3m and made 50 appearances, scoring seven goals.

Tijjani Reijnders is leaving Manchester City after just one season

Clarets land Coudet

Burnley have signed goalkeeper Gregoire Coudet from French side Brest on a permanent deal. The 27-year-old has signed a four-year contract.

Norwich City have signed Fenerbahce winger Anthony Musaba on a season's loan.

The Championship club will pay a proportion of the 25-year-old's salary after finding a replacement for Ali Ahmed following his knee injury.

Toffees consider Cash grab

Everton are showing interest in Aston Villa right back Matty Cash as they assess all options in the market.

Villa are signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka from West Ham today and he is being brought in to increase competition for Cash in the right-back berth. Poland international Cash has three years left on contract.

Everton have been working through a raft of names to try and solve their issue at right-back which has even prompted questions from Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

Barca keep tabs on Kane

Barcelona are monitoring Harry Kane's contract talks with Bayern Munich.

The England captain is giving priority to resolving his future with the German champions where he is settled and discussions are ongoing about the length of deal for the 33-year-old.

Kane is understood to want a three year deal and, as Daily Mail Sport revealed earlier this summer, Barca have made their interest known.

Read the full story here.

Villa braced for another Watkins bid

Aston Villa anticipate a fourth bid from Al Hilal for striker Ollie Watkins. The England international is open to the move but so far Villa have rejected their advances and want to keep the 30-year-old.

Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins is understood to be open to a move to Saudi Arabia

The latest bid of £38m was rejected on Tuesday evening. Villa maintain interested in Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson and have confirmed the signings of Matteo Ruggeri and Zion Suzuki.

Left back Ruggeri, 24, joins from Atletico Madrid, while goalkeeper Suzuki, 23, arrives after two years in Italy with Parma.

Meanwhile, Rangers have signed right back Kosta Nedeljkovic from Villa.

The 20-year-old has moved to Ibrox on a season-long loan, with a £4m obligation to buy, which will be triggered by the number of games he plays.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed last week, Villa are signing Aaron Wan Bissaka on loan from West Ham pending his medical today.

The deal can become an obligation to buy at around £18million.

There's a new Cherif in town

Coventry have completed their ninth signing of the summer transfer window with Fenerbahce striker Sidiki Cherif for £20.5million.

The deal has taken the club's spending to over £120m.

The 19-year-old, who was a target for Crystal Palace and Wrexham in January, made appearances in the Europa League and in this season’s Champions League qualifiers prior to opening talks with Coventry.

Toon's Nkunku offer

Newcastle have been offered the chance to sign former Chelsea forward Christopher Nkunku from AC Milan.

However, their priority remains to sign a midfielder first hence talks with Man City for Nico Gonzalez. Other targets are also being discussed.

Nkunku has been told he can leave Milan and has interest from RB Leipzig among others.

... and they're closing in on Diabate

Newcastle are also closing on Genclerbirligi’s midfielder Ousmane Diabate.

The highly-rated 18-year-old had been set for Brentford while Tottenham had also shown interest.

However, Newcastle look to have won the race with the teenager likely to stay on loan in Turkey for another season.

Diabate, a defensive midfielder, has played 10 matches for the U19s and seven for Genclerbirligi’s first team so far.

Liverpool defensive prospect in talks over La Liga move

Liverpool defensive prospect Ifeanyi Ndukwe is in talks to join Levante on loan.

The 18-year-old does not qualify for a work permit in England so is having to be loaned out.

The Austrian youth international has excelled during Liverpool's pre-season and the club have high hopes for his future.

First team football in a top league such as La Liga is viewed as an integral next step. He also has interest from Portugal and Germany.

Winger Kieran Morrison is joining Sheffield Wednesday on loan today.

Liverpool continue to discuss a move for Bradley Barcola at Paris St Germain but a deal for his teammate Ibrahim Mbaye is unlikely.

Konsa nearing Arsenal move...

Arsenal have agreed a £51million deal plus add-ons for Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa.

The England international has said goodbyes to staff at Villa and is due to undergo a medical tomorrow.

Read the full story here.

...as Gunners seek deal for United youngster

Arsenal are also working on a deal for 20-year-old right back Habeeb Ogunneye from Manchester United.

Arsenal want players to boost their U21s squad and have also shown interest in United's James Scanlon.

Gibraltar international winger Scanlon was on loan at Swindon Town last season.

England youth international Ogunneye had a spell at Newport on loan.

Baleba close to United switch

Manchester United are closing on a £65million deal for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba.

Talks resumed for the Cameroon international in recent weeks after it became apparent his ankle ligament injury was not as serious as first feared.

Read the full story here.

Pogba tears up Monaco deal

Monaco have confirmed that Paul Pogba has left by mutual agreement, bringing his time at the Ligue 1 club to a premature end.

The 33-year-old former Manchester United midfielder is now a free agent and has been offered to clubs in the MLS.

Read the full story here.

Paul Pogba's time at Monaco is over - with MLS clubs now considering a move for the former Man United midfielder

Farke reunites with Elvedi

Leeds have signed Nico Elvedi from Borussia Monchengladbach. The final fee is £6.5m rising to £8.5m with bonuses.

The 29-year-old Switzerland international centre back worked with Daniel Farke previously at the Bundesliga club.

James set for Wolves move

Rennes midfielder Jordan James is poised to finalise his move to Wolves today pending his medical.

The Wales international midfielder is joining on an initial loan deal with an option to sign permanently for around £10m.

He impressed on loan at Leicester last season scoring 11 goals in 34 games and had interest from Middlesbrough and West Ham.

Chelsea defender closes on Italy move

Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile has arrived at Villa Stuart in Rome ahead of his medical this morning.

The 25-year-old centre back is joining Napoli on loan for around £2.5m with an option for the deal to become permanent at £23m.

Mamadou Sarr, meanwhile, is emerging as a target for Real Sociedad and Al Hilal.

The 20-year-old has been expected to go on loan in the Premier League and interest there remains.

The Senegal international was recalled from a loan at Strasbourg to provide cover last season and started in their FA Cup win over Hull.

Piroe party at West Ham

West Ham have signed Joel Piroe on loan from Leeds until the end of the season.

The deal also includes an option for it to become permanent, which will be activated should certain conditions be met, including West Ham winning promotion back to the Premier League.

Joel Piroe has joined West Ham on loan from Leeds

West Ham turned to 27-year-old Piroe after hitting an impasse in talks for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott who is joining Real Betis for £17m plus add ons.

Piroe, who has scored 73 goals in the Championship during spells with Leeds and Swansea , said: 'I see West Ham as a Club that really wants to be in the Premier League, and I think should be in the Premier League.

'With my experience, I think I can help the Club a lot to achieve what they want to achieve, and I think it’s a good opportunity for me to show what I’ve learnt and how I’ve grown as a football player over the years.'

Piroe finished the 2024-25 season as the Championship's top scorer, helping Leeds United earn promotion to the Premier League.

The Hammers remain an option for free agent Jamie Vardy.

Potters snare Ipswich pair

Stoke have agreed a fee of around £6million with Ipswich for striker George Hirst and are also taking Ipswich full back Ben Johnson on loan.

Scotland international Hirst is to undergo medical later today. The fee will increase on performance related bonuses.

Sports.title: Brighton's gifts from the Arctic Circle: Lewis Dunk and Co reward 407 hardy fans travelling for Euro clash in Tromso with free tickets and merchandise
Sports.content:
Brighton's gifts from the Arctic Circle: Lewis Dunk and Co reward 407 hardy fans travelling for Euro clash in Tromso with free tickets and merchandise

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Brighton’s players have paid for tickets, T-shirts and scarves for more than 400 supporters who have travelled into the Arctic Circle to see them play against Tromso.

Captain Lewis Dunk explained why the players wanted to thank loyal fans ahead of the first leg of the Conference League play-off in Norway on Thursday.

'The fans didn’t know where they were going to go until the last minute,' said Dunk.

'It’s a long trip and last-minute to organise so we as a group of players wanted to make a gesture by refunding their tickets and give them a little present.

'Hopefully they appreciate it and it’s the start of a good season and we all enjoy it along the way.'

Brighton are back in Europe for their second campaign. They reached the last 16 of the Europa League in 2023-24 losing to Roma after winning a group featuring Ajax, Marseille and AEK Athens.

Lewis Dunk and Co rewarded Brighton fans by refunding their tickets for the Tromso clash

They have sold 407 tickets for the first leg at Tromso, who beat Cluj of Romania last week to set up the tie with Brighton.

'We’re not coming here and thinking it’s going to be easy,' said Dunk. 'It’s two games for a season’s work and we want to qualify for this competition.

'It’s the first game of the season. We’ve had a great pre-season and we’re raring to go.

'We’re an established Premier League side, finished high up in the table a lot of the time.

'We’d back ourselves against anyone in this competition. Let’s hope it goes well, we take a result back home and finish the job next week.'

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
